Notice how many European passports on this map are the same deep red. It's less a coincidence than a negotiated standard.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ Passport design in the EU is harmonised by recommendation, not by directive. Member states agreed the common burgundy cover by consensus, following a Resolution dated 23 June 1981.
2/ The result: every EU member state's ordinary passport is burgundy-red, with one exception. Croatia kept a dark blue cover when it redesigned its passport in August 2015.
3/ The UK shows how this can flip. After Brexit, British passports went back to navy blue, a design first used in 1921, with non-EU navy passports issued from March 2020.
4/ Outside the EU, other colours appear on the map. Russia's is red, Switzerland's is red with a white cross, while Ukraine's and Belarus's are blue.
5/ Standardisation of passports began around 1980 under the ICAO. Outside the EU's own recommendation, nothing forces a colour, which is why this map still shows plenty of variety.
6/ Why burgundy specifically? The sources I checked don't say, which is part of the charm. It stuck because uniformity was the point, and the colour was a convenient consensus.
7/ Which passport on this map is your favourite design? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
